title: Senior asks: a user saves a price 0.1 + 0.2 in a JSON file with write(). What is stored?
explain: json_encode() writes the exact float. In PHP, 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004 (binary floats). Your API stores what it gets, so it is fine for a file tool. For money, use integers (cents) or strings, not floats.

title: CsvFileActions::read() gives all values as strings. The jQuery page sorts the ids. What does Node print?
explain: CSV values are strings. sort() without a compare function sorts as text, so '10' comes before '2'. Fix: convert before sorting, for example sort((a, b) => a - b), which converts the strings to numbers.

title: Senior asks: your getFileName() uses basename(). What do these calls return?
explain: basename('..') returns .. and basename('a/..') is '..' too. basename('/') is ''. It cuts the folder part, but it does not remove the name '..'. The path storage/.. is a directory, so is_file() is false and the user gets 404. Safe here, but check is_file() and the extension.

title: Senior asks: write() uses LOCK_EX. Anna and Ben both read fruits.csv, both edit, both write back. What is the result?
options: Ben's write replaces Anna's edit, no error
explain: LOCK_EX stops two writes at the same moment, so the file is never half-written. It does not stop a lost update: each client sends the full file, and the last write wins. Fix ideas: ETag with If-Match (answer 412 if changed), or a version field in the data.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: empty() is true for '0' (the string zero), but not for '0.0'. Only '' and '0' are falsy strings. Never use empty() to check an input that can be 0. Use $x === '' or $x === null.

title: AI wrote items.map(async x => x * 2). What does Node print?
explain: An async function always returns a Promise, even for a plain value. map() puts the promises in the array, it does not wait. To get the numbers, use await Promise.all(items.map(async ...)). A common bug in AI code.

title: PHP 8.2. A readonly array property and an add() method. What does this print?
options: Cannot indirectly modify readonly property Cart::$items
explain: readonly means the property can be set only once, inside the class. $this->items[] = $x changes the array inside it, so PHP throws an Error. Fix: return a new object with the new array (a 'with' method): new self([...$this->items, $x]).

verify.expect: Cannot indirectly modify readonly property Cart::$items

title: You deploy a Symfony app to the production server. Which command installs the packages?
explain: install uses composer.lock, so production gets the same versions as your tests. --no-dev skips PHPUnit and other tools, so the server is smaller and safer. --optimize-autoloader makes the class loading faster. update would change versions on the server.
